\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ethe Hutt family legacy, and much more!\u003c/span\u003e","summary":"\u003ch2\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHow a Y-wing connects \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e to\u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e Star Wars: A New Hope, \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ethe Hutt family legacy, and much more!\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e","main_content":"\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eKeep these Easter eggs out of Grogu’s reach, he might think they’re snacks!\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eFor instance, did you know that Rotta the Hutt wasn’t always a muscled fighter? While he made his live-action debut in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, now streaming on Disney+, the character was actually introduced as a baby nearly 20 years ago in the first animated theatrical tale from \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/series/star-wars-the-clone-wars\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Clone Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e. \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHarkening back to his roots, the film — now streaming on Disney+ — also includes a live-action holo image of baby Rotta, courtesy of a model hand painted by Director Jon Favreau himself.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"mh-youtube mh-youtube-responsive\"\u003e\u003ciframe src=\"https://www.youtube.com/embed/8QXu4PLRLt0\" frameborder=\"0\" allow=\"accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share\" allowfullscreen=\"true\"\u003e\u003c/iframe\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eRead on to uncover more Easter eggs and fun facts from the film, including behind-the-scenes trivia from \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu Official Podcast\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, with all episodes now on Disney+.\u003c/span\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-rotta-the-hu_6d39fac9.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Rotta the Huttlet first appeared in the Star Wars: The Clone Wars animated film directed by Dave Filoni.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e1. \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/rotta-the-huttlet\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Rotta the Huttlet\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eRotta the Huttlet\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e first appeared in the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Clone Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e animated film directed by Dave Filoni. The 2008 feature launched the series by the same name and introduced Jabba the Hutt’s son, nicknamed Stinky, as well as \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/anakin-skywalker\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Anakin Skywalker\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAnakin Skywalker\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e’s Padawan \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/ahsoka-tano\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Ahsoka Tano\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAhsoka Tano\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-jeremy-allen_782f2c52.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"A final frame of Rotta and an image of Jeremy Allen White.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e2. David Acord originally voiced baby Rotta in animation. For the film, the older Rotta is performed by Jeremy Allen White (\u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Bear\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e) and Acord serves as sound designer.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-the-twins_10ff1527.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The Twins in Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu and Star Wars: The Book of Boba Fett.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e3. \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-twins\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"The Twins\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThe Twins\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e first appeared in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/series/the-book-of-boba-fett\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Star Wars: The Book of Boba Fett\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Book of Boba Fett\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-tippett-hutt_8f2cf506.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Phil Tippett headed the creature shop for Star Wars: Return of the Jedi, designing several creatures including Jabba the Hutt, the original template that all Hutts, like the Twins and Rotta, are based on.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e4. During his time with Lucasfilm, Phil Tippett headed the creature shop for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/star-wars-episode-vi-return-of-the-jedi\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: Return of the Jedi\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, designing several creatures including Jabba the Hutt, the original template that all Hutts, like the Twins and Rotta, are based on.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-droid-guardi_f4264343.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The giant droids guarding the Twins’ palace to life\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e5. After \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eJedi,\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Tippett founded Tippett Studios, where stop-motion animators have worked on sequences for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e and \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eSkeleton Crew\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, most recently lending their skill to bring the giant droids guarding the Twins’ palace to life.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-tippett-deja_b12fb84e.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The dejarik chess creatures in The Mandalorian and Grogu and A New Hope.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e6. Tippett was also the co-creator and animator of the dejarik chess creatures first seen in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: A New Hope\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, and now found rampaging through Shakari in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-embo_8c8213fd.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Embo the Kyozo first appeared in the Star Wars: The Clone Wars animated series during the Season 2 episode, “Bounty Hunters.”\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e7. \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/embo\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Embo\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eEmbo\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e the Kyozo first appeared in the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Clone Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e animated series during the Season 2 episode, “Bounty Hunters.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-marrok_414d1900.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Embo's anoobas.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e8. Although he previously worked with an \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/anooba\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Anooba\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eanooba\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e named Marrok in animation, the creature seen prowling with Embo in live-action is a different member of the same species. Her name is Keibu.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-anzellons-ba_f892e2a3.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The Anzellan Droidsmiths and Babu Frik.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e9. Actor Shirley Henderson, who voiced the first Anzellan, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/babu-frik\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Babu Frik\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBabu Frik\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-rise-of-skywalker\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Rise of Skywalker\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, and provided the voices for the trio of droidsmiths in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eSeason 3, returns to voice all four Anzellans — Minch, Bai, Keeto, and newcomer Clang.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-wayne-crowde_3e03b5f4.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"(L-R) Brendan Wayne and Lateef Crowder attend The Mandalorian and Grogu Los Angeles World Premiere.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003e(L-R) Brendan Wayne and Lateef Crowder attend The Mandalorian and Grogu Los Angeles World Premiere.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e10. Stunt Performer / Stunt Fight Coordinator Lateef Crowder is a two-time Emmy winner for outstanding stunt performance for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. He is also one of three people to wear the Mandalorian’s armor in the film. Crowder shares the helmet with Brendan Wayne and Pedro Pascal.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-cweathers_39a7651e.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"A sign above the doorway leading to the dejarik arena says “Weathers Apollo” in an homage to the late Greef Karga actor Carl Weathers who famously portrayed Apollo Creed in the Rocky franchise.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e11. A sign above the doorway leading to the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/dejarik\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Dejarik\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003edejarik\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e arena says “Weathers Apollo” in an homage to the late \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/greef-karga\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Greef Karga\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eGreef Karga\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e actor Carl Weathers who famously portrayed Apollo Creed in the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRocky\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e franchise.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-shakari_90040380.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Shakari\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e12. The design for the Moon of Shakari resembles Prohibition-era Chicago and was inspired by Director Jon Favreau’s time in the real city.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-dejarik_10f75e61.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The Dejarik Match is an homage to the holochess game.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e13. The Dejarik Match is an homage to the holochess game first played in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/star-wars-episode-iv-a-new-hope\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Star Wars: A New Hope\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: A New Hope\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"The Mandalorian and Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eestablishes that the \u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003ecreatures seen in the game version are indeed real beasts that can be seen fighting in the Pit on Shakari.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-mudhorn-egg_7f2b94d1.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Hugo Durant keeps a mudhorn egg in his stall. Fans may remember another mudhorn egg that featured prominently in Season 1 of The Mandalorian, in Chapter 2 “The Child.”\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e14. Sooga! Hugo Durant keeps a \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/mudhorn\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"mudhorn\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003emudhorn\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e egg in his stall. Fans may remember another mudhorn egg that featured prominently in Season 1 of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian,\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/series/the-mandalorian/chapter-2-guide\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eChapter 2 “The Child.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-y-wing_6fe5c4a9.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The Red Jammer Y-wing.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e15. The model of the Red Jammer Y-wing used in the film was borrowed from the\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003e archives. Crafted for the original film,\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003e the model was used as reference for the full-sized Y-wings in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/star-wars-episode-iv-a-new-hope\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: A New Hope\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e but has never previously been used on screen.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-pilots_09fd9eb3.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"A few of the New Republic recruits on Adelphi Base include Lucasfilm President and Chief Creative Officer Dave Filoni as Trapper Wolf, Lucasfilm Art Department’s Doug Chiang and Michelle Thieme, as well as episodic directors Deborah Chow, Lee Isaac Chung, and Rick Famuyiwa.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e16. A few of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-new-republic\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003ethe New Republic\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e recruits found on Adelphi Base have also helped bring \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eto life behind the scenes. Look closely to find Lucasfilm President and Chief Creative Officer Dave Filoni as Trapper Wolf, Lucasfilm Art Department’s Doug Chiang and Michelle Thieme, as well as episodic directors Deborah Chow, Lee Isaac Chung, and Rick Famuyiwa.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-lord-janu_99941dfa.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Lord Janu’s office walls.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e17. Some things you may have noticed on the walls of Lord Janu’s office walls: a \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/nexu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003enexu\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/vexis\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003evexis\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/reek\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003ereek\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, and barghest!\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-daniels_48e1b682.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The Air Traffic Control droids\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e18. Oh dear. Listen carefully and you may recognize the voice of Anthony Daniels, the longtime performer behind \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/c-3po\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eC-3PO\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. In \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e he voices the Air Traffic Control droids who give the Mandalorian, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eGrogu\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, and Zeb clearance to land on Nal Hutta to meet with the Twins.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-rotta-concep_e44f0dc8.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e19. Jon Favreau hand painted the concept art model of Rotta the Huttlet, he even signed his name at the bottom.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-hutt_29cd790a.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Adult Rotta has the anchor-shaped tattoo of his family clan on the back of his head.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e20. Adult Rotta has the anchor-shaped tattoo of his family clan on the back of his head.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-moon_db43bfc3.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Seen orbiting Nal Hutta is a city-covered moon, a nod to Nar Shaddaa, the famous Smuggler’s Moon first featured in Star Wars comics in the 1990s.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e21. Seen orbiting Nal Hutta is a city-covered moon, a nod to Nar Shaddaa, the famous Smuggler’s Moon first featured in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ecomics in the 1990s.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-adelphi-base_4d6bfa1e.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e22. There are several recognizable droids and helmets lining the bar at Adelphi Base, with parts of a probe droid, a \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/mouse-droid\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003emouse droid\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, and a discarded TIE pilot helmet among them.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-fuzzball_c5c45e15.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Fuzzball locked in one of the cages at the Salt Bar.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e23. Look closely and you may spot \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/Fuzzball\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eFuzzball\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e locked in one of the cages at the Salt Bar. Fuzzball was recently seen in episode 2 of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/series/star-wars-skeleton-crew\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: Skeleton Crew\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e and was first seen in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eCaptain EO\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, a now defunct science fiction musical previously shown at Walt Disney Parks.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-snack_6dd48aea.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e24. The popcorn-like snack Grogu eats during Rotta’s match is a ringer for Mantell Mix seen in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/series/star-wars-the-bad-batch\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Bad Batch\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eand Outpost Mix available for snacking when you visit \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: Galaxy’s Edge \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eat Disneyland and Walt Disney World resorts.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-rifle_bc41d249.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Din Djarin arms himself with a new Amban rifle.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e25. While gathering weapons, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-mandalorian\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eDin Djarin\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e arms himself with a new Amban rifle. More ornate than the version seen in Season 1, the weapon is a nod to the one carried by \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/boba-fett\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBoba Fett\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e in his first appearance on screen in “The Story of the Faithful \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/wookiee\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eWookiee\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e,” an animated short that debuted in the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars Holiday Special.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-sword_874a2a11.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Din has to choose from one of the arena weapons.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e26. One of the arena weapons Din has to choose from is modeled off the Blades of Chaos used by Kratos in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eGod of War.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-filming_484ee3a6.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e27. Director Jon Favreau voiced \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/rio-durant\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eRio Durant\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e for 2018’s \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/solo\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eSolo: A Star Wars Story\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, the first appearance of the same Ardennian alien species as the Martin Scorsese-voiced Hugo Durant.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-food-cookboo_01f813ae.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The labeled food items in Hugo’s food pod.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e28 Among the labeled food items in Hugo’s food pod are containers of “Arkanian Tenderloin,” “Lira San Crackers” and “Lammas Tree Bites,” all from 2023’s \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Ultimate Cookbook.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-blurrg_aabcbf04.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Mando’s homestead on Nevarro includes a paddock with a pair of blurrgs.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e29. Mando’s homestead on \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/nevarro\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eNevarro\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e includes a paddock with a pair of blurrgs, a creature last seen in Season 1 of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-razor-crest_d1a9414b.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The 48-inch physical model created for motion control VFX shots of the new Razor Crest.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e30. Both a two-foot and four-foot physical model were created for motion control VFX shots of the new \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/razor-crest\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"mh-youtube mh-youtube-responsive\"\u003e\u003ciframe src=\"https://www.youtube.com/embed/fwqguHvfG2Y\" frameborder=\"0\" allow=\"accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share\" allowfullscreen=\"true\"\u003e\u003c/iframe\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e31. Real-life chef Roy Choi created the flat-meat sandwich for Hugo Durant’s food pod on Shakari.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-int-4-vehicl_0a3d66f9.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The INT-4 vehicle that the Imperial warlord uses to escape the AT-AT walker is based on the 1982 Kenner Mini-Rig toy of the same name.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e32. The INT-4 vehicle that the Imperial warlord uses to escape the AT-AT walker is based on the 1982 Kenner Mini-Rig toy of the same name.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-turtle-tank_a99053a7.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Turte Tanker\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e33. A \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/turtle-tanker\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTurtle Tanker\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, like the one Rotta the Hutt departs Nevarro in, first appeared in Season 4 of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Clone Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e in the episode \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/series/clone-wars/brothers-episode-guide\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“Brothers.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-nal-hutta_0356126e.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e34. Nal Hutta’s first canonical \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eappearance was in the Season 3 \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Clone Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e episode “Hunt for Ziro.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-imperial-shu_0fce4de4.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The Hutt fighter was inspired by a 1981 Imperial Shuttle design by Return of the Jedi production designer Norman Reynolds.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e35. The Hutt fighter was inspired by a 1981 \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/imperial-shuttle\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eImperial Shuttle\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e design by \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/star-wars-episode-vi-return-of-the-jedi\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eReturn of the Jedi\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eproduction designer Norman Reynolds.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-barro_ee8fd09b.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Warlord Commander Barro\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e36. Warlord Commander Barro (Hemky Madera) was previously glimpsed in the holographic meeting of the Shadow Council in season 3 of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-at-at-helmet_96daec0f.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The AT-AT driver helmets were cast in light gray, matching what was done for The Empire Strikes Back.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e37. The AT-AT driver helmets were cast in light gray, matching what was done for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/star-wars-episode-v-the-empire-strikes-back\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Empire Strikes Back\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e. \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eFor years, many assumed them to be white, because of inaccurate lighting of behind-the-scenes photography. The original AT-AT driver armor was repainted black to serve as background \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/tie-fighter\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTIE fighter\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e pilots for the hangar scenes in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eReturn of the Jedi.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-whistling-bi_8f957ce3.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e38. Mando lost his \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/whistling-birds\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003ewhistling birds\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e launcher from his left gauntlet at the end of Season 3 of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eand has not replaced them.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-landis_53955dd5.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Landis Fields and a final frame of Colonel Ward.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e39. Chief Evo, the ground crew tech who takes Colonel Ward’s helmet is played by Industrial Light \u0026amp; Magic's Landis Fields.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-amani_b4d51da4.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Amani\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e40. The idea that \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/amani\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAmani\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e can move quickly by rolling is derived from a description in the original roleplaying game supplement that gave them their name, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eGalaxy Guide 12: Aliens – Enemies and Allies\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, published in 1995.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-podcast-imax_f0e7dcd6.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1440\" alt=\"A 4:3 IMAX frame from The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e41. Sets for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e were built to accommodate the film’s taller 4:3 IMAX aspect ratio, compared to the more horizontal 2:35 aspect ratio used in television and other \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e media. \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"mh-youtube mh-youtube-responsive\"\u003e\u003ciframe src=\"https://www.youtube.com/embed/Hu_QV1HQ2rs\" frameborder=\"0\" allow=\"accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share\" allowfullscreen=\"true\"\u003e\u003c/iframe\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e42. During the film’s press tour, Grogu had his own press junket room for reporters to come in with their questions. The young star also attended the Oscars!\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-podcast-pupp_1de0210c.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Dave Filoni served as second unit director for The Mandalorian and Grogu, overseeing the puppet unit.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e43. Dave Filoni served as second unit director for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, overseeing the puppet unit that brought Grogu and his Anzellans friends to life.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-podcast-ludw_423957b8.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"Donald Glover — who played young Lando Calrissian in Solo: A Star Wars Story — recommended Ludwig Göransson to Jon Favreau.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e44. Donald Glover — who played young Lando Calrissian in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/solo\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eSolo: A Star Wars Story\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e— recommended Ludwig Göransson to Jon Favreau after the composer collaborated on Glover’s hit single, “This Is America.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-podcast-hugo_904bbc47.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The radio in Hugo Durant’s snack shack quietly plays an uptempo guitar arrangement of the main theme from The Mandalorian\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e45. The radio in Hugo Durant’s snack shack quietly plays an uptempo guitar arrangement of the main theme from \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ewhile the four-armed alien gets to work in his food pod.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eDin Djarin and Grogu embark on their most thrilling mission yet in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. Directed by Jon Favreau and filmed for IMAX, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e stars Pedro Pascal as the Mandalorian, Sigourney Weaver as Colonel Ward, and Jeremy Allen White as Rotta the Hutt. The film is written by Jon Favreau, Dave Filoni, and Noah Kloor, and is produced by Kathleen Kennedy, Ian Bryce, Jon Favreau, and Dave Filoni, with Karen Gilchrist, John Bartnicki, and Carrie Beck serving as executive producers and music by Ludwig Göransson.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/rotta-the-huttlet\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Rotta the Hutt\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eRotta the Hutt\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e know, but there \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eis \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eone way that he is quite similar to his late father — and it is a perfect time to call it out, now that \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eis streaming on Disney+ and available on digital and 4K Ultra HD.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIn 1997’s Special Edition of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/star-wars-episode-iv-a-new-hope\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Star Wars: A New Hope\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: A New Hope\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, viewers witnessed as smuggler \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/han-solo\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Han Solo\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHan Solo\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e walked behind a computer graphics \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/jabba-the-hutt\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Jabba the Hutt\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eJabba the Hutt\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e and stepped on his tail. And so while Rotta might be nothing like his old man, he is also no stranger to getting his personal space trampled upon. “It goes by super fast, but there is actually a moment during their fight when Mando circles behind Rotta, steps on his tail to get a little height, and then knocks his arm out of the way,” Hal Hickel, a long-time ILM animation supervisor, reveals to StarWars.com.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“We didn't put that in there as a wink to the original gag, but still – it's like poetry, it rhymes.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/the-making-of-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-rotta-the-hutt-_4db31dc1.jpeg?region=0,0,1280,541\" alt=\"Rotta the Huttlett riding around in Ahsoka Tano’s backpack.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eMany longtime fans met Rotta before the premiere of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"The Mandalorian and Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, during the late summer of 2008. At the time of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Clone Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eanimated film’s debut, Jabba the Hutt’s son was no more than a little green blob nicknamed “Stinky” and riding around in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/ahsoka-tano\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Ahsoka Tano\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAhsoka Tano\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e’s backpack. In fact, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Clone Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003emovie was \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003ealso\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e the young Torgruta Padawan’s debut into a galaxy far, far away. Nearly 20 years later, both of these characters have grown up rather considerably, and now both have been adapted into live action, with Rotta re-appearing on the big screen as one of the main characters of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eand Ahsoka helming her own series \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/news/ahsoka-season-2\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003estarring Rosario Dawson, with Season 2 arriving early next year\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eOnce again, Rotta is a movie star — but it took a whole new team of artists to get him ready for his close-up.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/the-making-of-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-rotta-the-hutt-_45fbc004.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1035\" alt=\"Rotta the Hutt concept art by Richard Lim.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eRotta the Hutt concept art by Richard Lim.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGrand Designs\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIt all began with Production Designer Doug Chiang’s concept art crew, who worked through many iterations of what a grown-up (and potentially less stinky) version of Rotta could look like. From there, the design was delivered to Industrial Light \u0026amp; Magic, starting with a digital iteration built by Lead Modeler Masa Narita and his team. Fortunately, Narita was already somewhat of a Hutt expert.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“I had actually worked on the Hutt Twins earlier for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Book of Boba Fett\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, so I used them as a starting point when work began on Rotta,” Narita says. “One of my key challenges was making Rotta clearly related to his uncles, while still feeling like a very different character. Even though they shared the same Hutt heritage, we wanted each character to have a distinct silhouette and personality, so a lot of the work was finding the right balance between family resemblance and individual character.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/the-making-of-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-rotta-the-hutt-_c9200eb3.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,960\" alt=\"Rotta the Hutt fighting in The Pits concept art by Richard Lim.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eRotta the Hutt fighting in The Pits concept art by Richard Lim.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eUnlike Rotta, who is young, strong, and athletic, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-twins\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"The Twins\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThe Twins\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e were designed to look much older and heavier. Their bodies were basically just masses of fat, with very little visible muscle definition. The ILM team wanted that contrast to help emphasize Rotta's youth and physical strength. As Narita explains: “For Rotta, we actually started from the brother Hutt's model. This allowed us to retain some of the facial shape libraries and design language that had already been established for the Hutt family. We then developed him into a much younger and stronger character.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHowever, Rotta could have looked quite different. At several points in the production process, Rotta’s design shifted as the final cut came together. “The original concept art gave Rotta a slightly scaly and intimidating look. I started building the model based on that first design,” remembers Narita. “Later, Director Jon Favreau felt that the character should look more gentle and approachable, so the concept team created another version with a softer expression. As the project evolved, the design continued to change.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/the-making-of-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-rotta-the-hutt-_63e241f4.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,960\" alt=\"Rotta the Hutt compared to Jabba the Hutt concept art by Richard Lim.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eRotta the Hutt compared to Jabba the Hutt concept art by Richard Lim.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHickel adds further context: “Right before shooting began, we had pretty much settled on the design — Rotta’s digital asset was underway at ILM, we had started to do some animation tests, and Legacy Effects had sculpted a full-size head for shooting reference. We were all in unison — myself, [Director] Jon Favreau, [Production Visual Effects Supervisor] John Knoll, and Doug Chiang. But after shooting finished and the dust had settled and the cut was assembling, a funny thing happened where we all started to question it. Ultimately we went back in and rolled up our sleeves and did a redesign, mostly on his face. [Lucasfilm President and Chief Creative Officer] Dave Filoni gave us really good insights: We had made him too friendly and too human. He didn't look ‘Hutt-y’ enough.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“He didn't look like his father's son,” Hickel adds, laughing. “Fortunately, Jon was the type of director who was very open to ideas and understood when something could be better or needs to change. He was not afraid to rip up the track and get in there. It wasn't so late in the process that it was disastrous — it was actually good timing — but for me, as a creative person, it was very interesting to have a doubt about something and then to actually pull it apart and fix it.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“It was really gratifying, and I loved where we ended up with Rotta.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-jon-favreau-intervi_d8688c40.jpeg?region=0,363,1920,1557\" alt=\"Rotta the Hutt in The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eI Like to Move It, Move It\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBut looks aren’t everything. “From an animation standpoint, Rotta was the hardest problem to solve in the whole film,” continues Hickel. “We had seen Hutts before, but generally they were big, sedentary villains like Jabba and the Twins. We hadn’t even really seen them moving around before, so just figuring out a credible walk for Rotta was challenging, let alone a credible way for him to move quickly and dangerously against an opponent.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eFor inspiration, the ILM team turned to the natural world, zeroing in on the elephant seal, which are the largest seals on Earth. “We came up with a run based on what elephant seals do,” says Hickel. “They run on their forward fins — their front hands — while the tail of their body does ‘the worm,’ undulating along. And then their big bodies sort of collide as they battle.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eEvery time Rotta was on screen, the completely digital creation had to nevertheless seem as real as the physical actors and on-set elements. “Our creature dev artists had to make him really feel solid, fleshy, and heavy,” continues Hickel, whose experience includes once serving as an animator for creatures like \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/watto\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Watto\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eWatto\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e and \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/boss-nass\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Boss Nass\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBoss Nass\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. “Inside our digital asset for Rotta, we built a skeleton, a muscle system, fat layers, and skin layers, and then they all got simulated after the animation had been done — muscles firing, tensing, and relaxing, with a jiggling fat layer on top. The skin layer really helped sell raw weight — when he does that big crushing move onto the gladiator and you see all that mass moving, it really helps you feel like, ‘Oh my gosh, that's 800 pounds of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003esomething\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e.’”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/the-making-of-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-rotta-the-hutt-_5bb6a282.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1280\" alt=\"The Rotta the Hutt head made by Legacy Effects.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eThe Rotta the Hutt head made by Legacy Effects. \u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eOn set Rotta was portrayed by Richard Cetrone, a member of the movie’s stunt team. “He was our ‘Rotta guy’ throughout the whole movie,” says Hickel. “Whenever Rotta was in the scene, Richard would be out there as the stand-in, so that we had a correct eyeline for Brendan Wayne, Lateef Crowder, or Pedro Pascal as Mando — whoever was physically in the scene. He could even carry that enormous Legacy Effects head if we needed him to, to give the camera operators a real sense of what this other character looked like. Rotta is not especially tall, he's only about the same height as a man, a little over six feet tall, but we still wanted to account for his bulk.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eFor ILM Digital Artist Meg Grube, it was always about making him heavy: “You never wanted him to feel like he was floating, or that he was too light on his non-existent feet. You always wanted to take him seriously. He's a tough opponent.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAbove all this physicality, however, it was equally important to properly convey Rotta’s emotions. He was not just an adversary, a monster, or a computer graphics creature — he is ultimately a sympathetic character that the audience has to care about. “He had the second-most lines of dialogue in the film, including three scenes with Mando that were just straight-up dialogue scenes with no action,” says Hickel. “These types of character-based scenes were hugely rewarding for our animators to get to do. We really got the best of both worlds with Rotta: action and emotion in the same character. It was super fun.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/the-making-of-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-rotta-the-hutt-_48f26c90.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,800\" alt=\"Rotta holding Grogu concept art by Christian Alzmann.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/the-making-of-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-rotta-the-hutt-_6bf073d4.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,804\" alt=\"Rotta meets Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAccording to Grube, it was perhaps most important to get his facial expressions down. She even went back to some cinematic places for inspiration: “I started to watch a lot of action movies, adding in that tough guy attitude from, say, a boxing film. But overall it really became a story of less is more,” explains Grube. “If you did too much, [Animation Supervisors] Hal Hickel and Rick O’Connor would be like, ‘Tone it down and bring this back,’ and that was when you really stripped it back to just a pose or a look. It ended up being much more successful.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eSo was there any real-life reference from Rotta’s voice actor Jeremy Allen White that animators took further cues from? Grube actually used several pieces from Rotta’s performers as examples. “There was a behind-the-scenes video of Jeremy that I watched: just the way he held himself when he yelled was useful for some shots,” remembers Grube. “Even the stunt actor who was on set (Richard Cetrone) had a way that he held himself or swung with a certain look on his face, and I actually found that useful too.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBut Hickel notes, “While Richard played the character on set, and Jeremy performed the voice, all emotion had to come from the animator.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-rotta-the-hutt-figh_55204d4e.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,804\" alt=\"Rotta fights in the Shakari arena known as the Pits.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLet Me Roll It\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAbove all, Rotta had to feel dangerous. As Grube puts it, “The best and worst things about working on Rotta was that you didn't know how he was going to move. In some ways, that was really intimidating and challenging. But then at the same time, it was great because you could take some really big swings and really establish this character.” It was this sort of unpredictability that further translated Rotta’s dynamism to the screen.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eOf course, Rotta couldn’t be a famed gladiator without a signature move. Luckily, ILM was the perfect tag-team for the job. “Early on during our work on the sequence, we received a note that Rotta wasn’t fighting in a way that felt distinct to the Hutts. He shouldn’t fight like a human but in a way unique to his own physicality,\" says Dave Logan, Lead Animator for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. “How should he attack? At this point in the cut, there was a lot more punching, nothing super specific about his movements for a Hutt. So the request came in to make him roll into an attack, because, you know, he's a slug. He should be able to roll, right?”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-rotta-the-hutt-aren_bb8e98a6.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,804\" alt=\"The Shakari arena known as the Pits.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“It became this thing we called the ‘Rotta Roll’ where he would just drop down flat on the ground and roll sideways, and he could do that pretty quickly,” Hickel describes. “He could get right up on an opponent very quickly, and overtake them. We also imagined that Rotta could spin his body around just to hit people with his tail — he catches Mando unaware quite early in their fight and sends him sprawling.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eWhile that might sound easy enough, Logan knew that it could quickly become quite complicated, so he gave it to Grube. “When I first heard the request, I had a hard time picturing how it could be done in a cool, interesting way,” says Logan. “We had Meg work on it, and when we first saw it, I was like, ‘Oh my god, she’s figured it out.’ We ended up using it a couple more times in the movie.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBut perhaps Rotta’s most impactful on-screen moment is a bit quieter than a punchy finishing move: the small scene of the young Hutt playing on the beach with little \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eGrogu\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. It is a moment of peace, not gladiator violence — a shared interaction between two alien creatures, conveying real aspects of human emotion. In other words, it is a moment of pure \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e magic.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“That was maybe the most important scene to Jon,” says Hickel. “It’s the heart of the whole movie for him.” You might just say: Rotta was the key to all of this.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e"},"publish_date":"September 2, 2026","publish_date_short":"Sep
