dads.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e","main_content":"\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eRegardless of the ways they come into your life, there is no denying that fathers and father figures are some of the most influential people in this or any galaxy. On full display with our favorite duo in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, in theaters now, they protect us and teach us to prepare us for the future. They mold us in ways we may never understand and for better or worse, leave a lasting impact.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHere are just a few of our favorite \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003edads who exemplify the compassion and complexities of fatherhood.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/quiz-sw-found-family-grogu-mando_9c995698.jpeg?region=0,0,1280,537\" alt=\"Grogu being held by Din.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\n\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDin\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e Djar\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ein\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e and \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGrogu\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e - \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003ci class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe Mandalorian\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e, \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003ci class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\n\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAs a longtime bounty h\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003eunter\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003e and first-time dad, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-mandalorian\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eDin Djarin\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e knows a thing or two about caring for precious cargo. Initially being tasked with capturing \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/grogu\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eGrogu\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e on a basic retrieval mission, Din Djarin ultimately chose to save the young child, rescuing the alien from the Imperial forces. Finding purpose and duty in protecting the foundling from harm, Din and Grogu formed a Clan of Two. It didn’t take long before Grogu (\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003eand his big brown eyes) \u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003echipped away at the ruthless mercenary’s cold exterior and uncovered an undeniable attachment between him and his Dadalorian.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-father-figure-din-d_7ffba57b.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1280\" alt=\"Din Djarin and Grogu work on the Razor Crest.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThe many adventures of Din and Grogu showcase their unwavering bond, including their latest journey to the big screen with \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e in theaters now. Having survived the obstacles of distance, several outside threats, and a lot of trauma, it is their love for one another that continues to push them forward. \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"The Mandalorian and Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e are proof that family knows no bounds.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/andor-211-k2so_22765577.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,797\" alt=\"K-2SO\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\n\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCassian Andor\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e and \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eK-\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2SO\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e - \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003ci class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAndor\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e, \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003ci class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRogue O\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ene: A S\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003etar Wars Story\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\n\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eFathers come in all shapes and sizes, and sometimes so do their kids. From the mind of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/k-2so-kay-tuesso\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eK-2SO\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e's actor himself, Alan Tudyk,\u003c/span\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/cassian-andor\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eCassian Andor\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e is, for all intents and purposes, K-2’s Papá. Though he was built by the Empire, it could be argued that K-2SO’s life didn’t really start until he woke up on \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/yavin-4\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Yavin 4\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eYavin 4\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e’s Rebel base, ready for a new life beyond his factory-original settings. Cassian saw potential in K-2SO, salvaging the damaged security droid from the rubble of the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/Ghorman\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Ghorman\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eGhorman\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Massacre, and believed that he could become more than his programming. Their shared experience of troubled and difficult pasts makes it easy to see why they became inseparable. The two relied on each other for more than just preservation. K-2SO came into Cassian’s life on the heels of a relentless string of devastating losses; as much as K-2SO needed guidance, Cassian needed companionship.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-father-figure-andor_1b51281d.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,804\" alt=\"Cassian Andor and K-2SO in Rogue One: A Star Wars Story.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eK-2’s quick wit and juvenile retorts are reminiscent of a child…an overly pragmatic and lethal child. However, K-2 ultimately showed a fierce loyalty and protective nature for the father figure in his life. Cassian Andor was the first person that K-2SO laid eyes on and the last. Together until the very end, Cassian and K-2SO lived and died for the rebellion and for each other.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/bad-batch-declassified-the-cavalry-has-arrived-mission-_7b665908.jpeg?region=0,0,1280,541\" alt=\"Omega and Hunter on Pabu\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\n\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHunter and \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOmega\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e - \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003ci class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStar Wars:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e The Bad Batch\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\n\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIn an era of change, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/hunter\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHunter\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e found an unlikely constant in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/omega\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eOmega\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. At first reluctant to bring the child into the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/elite-squad\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Elite Squad\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eElite Squad\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e known as Clone Force 99 or the Bad Batch, it didn’t take long until he and the young clone established an undeniable bond. Forged in the chaos of the rising Empire, it became evident that Omega needed Hunter just as much as he did her. While Hunter taught Omega how to be a soldier, she showed him how to find wonder in the mundane and forced him to question his oftentimes fixed perspectives. Of course, this ebb and flow of understanding didn’t come without its growing pains, every disagreement and concern drawing the pair closer through learned experiences.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/the-bb-s3-epguide-trivia-315-07_1932460b.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The epilogue features an older Omega, Hunter, and Batcher. Among their new looks is a Bad Batch skull patch on Omega’s jacket and a collar around Batcher’s neck.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHaving to navigate newfound dynamics is never easy (in any galaxy), which is why it couldn’t have been done without the collective effort of the Dad Batch. And although no father is ever ready to see their little one leave, there is no denying that this band of brothers couldn’t be prouder of their kid. After all, they will always be there to protect her and make sure she finds her way back home.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-lightsaber-battles-esb-luke-darth-vader_99b783fe.jpeg?region=0,0,1934,806\" alt=\"Luke Skywalker confrontations Darth Vader in The Empire Strikes Back.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\n\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDa\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003erth V\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eader\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e and \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLuke S\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ekywal\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eker\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e - \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003ci class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStar Wars: The Empir\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ee Strikes\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e Back\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e, \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003ci class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStar \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWars: Ret\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eurn of the Jedi\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\n\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTheir father-son relationship is complicated, to say the least, but when push comes to shove (or in this case, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/force-lightning\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Force Lightning\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eForce Lightning\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e), Daddy Darth knows when to pull through. Having grown up in the care of his \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/owen-lars\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eUncle Owen\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e and \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/beru-lars\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAunt Beru\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/luke-skywalker\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eLuke Skywalker\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e only knew partial truths about who his father really was. It wasn’t until their tumultuous confrontation on \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/bespin\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Bespin\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBespin\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e that Luke discovered the truth surrounding father's identity; \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/darth-vader\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eDarth Vader\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e’s iconic words “No, I am your father” changed all of our lives for good. This revelation not only sent Luke into a journey of self-discovery, but also left him to grapple with the newfound perception of his father and \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-force\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"the Force\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003ethe Force\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-rotj-quotes-luke-darth-vader_86d450b1.jpeg?region=0,0,1280,535\" alt=\"“You already have, Luke. You were right about me. Tell your sister...you were right.” Vader.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eUltimately, faith and conviction are what bring the two back together. Believing in the man he knew his father to be, Luke committed himself to the light side and guided \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/anakin-skywalker\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Anakin Skywalker\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAnakin Skywalker\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e back home. Even if just for his final moments, Anakin understood what it meant to be a dad — placing love and compassion over everything, his sacrifice saved his son and, ultimately,  the galaxy.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-father-figure-leia-_a99200ce.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1268\" alt=\"Bail Organa and Leia Organa in Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\n\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBail Or\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003egana\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e and \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eL\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eeia Org\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eana\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e - \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003ci class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStar Wars: Rev\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eenge o\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ef the Sith\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e, \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003ci class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eObi-W\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ean Keno\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ebi\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e, \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003ci class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRogue One: A Star Wars Story\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\n\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eA senator of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/alderaan\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Alderaan\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAlderaan\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, a founding member of the Rebellion, and an architect of Fulcrum, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/bail-organa\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBail Organa\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e was many things, but his most important role was arguably as father to \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/leia-organa\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eLeia Organa\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. Following the birth of the Skywalker twins, Bail didn’t hesitate in making the decision to adopt Leia with his wife, Breha Organa, and raise her as their own. From the moment they met, Bail never faltered in ensuring that his daughter knew she was wanted and loved.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-father-figure-leia-_43a8e290.jpeg?region=0,0,1908,778\" alt=\"Leia talks to Rey in The Force Awakens.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eRooted in endless devotion for each other and the Rebellion, the Organa family ingrained in Leia a deep sense of justice and compassion. The young princess grew up as a beacon of hope within the Rebellion, and although her father perished at the hands of the Empire, Leia devoted her life to continuing his legacy of justice and putting an end to oppressive forces everywhere.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/rotta-the-hutt-main_b939d6a9.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1280\" alt=\"Rotta the Hutt\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\n\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHonorable Mention: \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cb \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003edoesn’t just mark the return of the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/razor-crest\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Razor Crest\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e. \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIt also resurrects an old-school filmmaking technique, one used decades ago to bring the original trilogy to life.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIn \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"The Mandalorian and Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e, \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-mandalorian\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Din Djarin\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eDin Djarin\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e (Pedro Pascal) acquires a new version of his iconic ship, after the original \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e (RIP) was destroyed in a shootout. As a thank-you for Mando’s service to \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-new-republic\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"the New Republic\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003ethe New Republic\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/Colonel-Ward\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Colonel Ward\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eColonel Ward\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e (Sigourney Weaver) gifts him a pristine, factory-condition \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest, \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eone\u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eseized from the collection of an ex-Imperial warlord.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-razor-crest-razor-c_728b4dc0.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1280\" alt=\"Din Djarin acquires a new version of his iconic ship, the Razor Crest.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBringing back the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003emeant that the film’s visual effects team also wanted to bring back physical modelmaking, a classic technique that was also used in\u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e The Mandalorian \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eDisney+ series. \u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIn addition to building a highly detailed digital asset for the ship, \u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003ethe Industrial Light \u0026amp; Magic team painstakingly built models of the ship, using a motion-control rig to shoot the miniatures. It’s exactly how the original trilogy crew filmed X-wings or the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/millennium-falcon\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Millennium Falcon\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eMillennium Falcon\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ein \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/star-wars-episode-iv-a-new-hope\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"A New Hope\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: A New Hope\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e, \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eusing the pioneering camera system known as the “Dykstraflex\u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“It was such an old school \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ething,” animation supervisor Hal Hickel says of working on \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. “I was just absolutely in nerd heaven.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHere, members of the film’s visual effects team from Industrial Light \u0026amp; Magic (ILM) reveal how they made the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003efly, marrying historic techniques with cutting-edge digital tech.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-razor-crest-the-man_ebfbb042.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1280\" alt=\"John Knoll and John Goodson with the original Razor Crest model from The Mandalorian Season 1.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eJohn Knoll and John Goodson with the original Razor Crest model from The Mandalorian Season 1.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eModel behavior\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIn development of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eMandalorian\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e series, the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ewas intended to be solely depicted with a digital model. But early on, director Jon Favreau suggested building a small, physical model of the ship to use as a lighting reference. (The \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest’s \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eshiny exterior makes it particularly difficult to light — more on that in a minute.) Once the model was built, the ILM team began wondering: Why not shoot the model for real, the way it was done on the original \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e?\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“Way back on Season 1, we had a good-looking CG version of the ship, but in some ways, the finish and the actual look of the metal felt a little conventional somehow,” Hickel explains. “Jon wanted to keep exploring. So, we thought, ‘Well, let’s build a simple metallic version and put it outside in a bunch of different lighting environments to see what it tells us about reflectivity.’ That led to: ‘Well, let’s make it more than a lighting model. Let’s make it a \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003enice\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e-looking model.’ And then: ‘Let’s actually shoot it.’”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eJohn Goodson constructed the original \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003emodel, which was about 24 inches long. Production Visual Effects Supervisor and ILM Executive Creative Director John Knoll then designed and built a motion-control rig for the camera, allowing him to film in gorgeous detail.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“It was a really shoestring guerilla operation,” Knoll remembers of filming the model for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eSeason 1. “We had John Goodson working out of his garage and building the model, and I was working out of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003emy \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003egarage, putting together a camera system to shoot it.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-razor-crest-bts-ilm_08ea563b.jpeg?region=0,0,1620,1080\" alt=\"The 48-inch Razor Crest model being filmed for Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eThe 48-inch Razor Crest model being filmed for Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu. \u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThe original version was a success, but for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu, \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eKnoll wanted to up the scale — literally. In addition to building a new version of the 24-inch model, the team also built a much larger 48-inch version. Each served a different purpose: The smaller model made it easier to shoot fast fly-bys through space, but the bigger version allowed for detailed closeups.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThe 48-inch version was also built with removable ramps and landing gear, allowing Knoll to photograph the ship both in flight and on the ground.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-razor-crest-adelphi_66460b3c.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,804\" alt=\"The Razor Crest on Adelphi Base.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“I didn’t want to just do shots of it that were flying shots,” Knoll explains. “When we first see the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest, \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ewhen Mando is introduced to this new model, we come around the corner, and there it is parked at \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/Adelphi-Base\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Adelphi Base\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAdelphi Base\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. I wanted to be able to do shots like that with the 48-inch model.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eEach miniature shot required meticulous preparation. Before Knoll and the team could shoot a single frame, animators would mock up each shot digitally, mapping out every miniscule camera move and every light source.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“We would effectively create a 3D scene that would replicate what we’d photograph in reality,” Visual Effects Supervisor Jeff Capogreco explains. “We’d put the same constraints so the animators couldn’t over-crank the motion or do things that wouldn’t allow the miniature to effectively work.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“For me, the challenge is always to make sure that the shot design has the kind of old-school vibe that Favreau likes,” Hickel adds. “[I did] a deep dive into why the spaceship shots in the original trilogy look the way they do. Design-wise, the way the ships move through the frame or the stars move, it’s a very particular look. If you look at \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Trek \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003emovies from that era, for instance, it’s a totally different aesthetic.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAfter each shot was mapped out digitally, Knoll could use that computer graphics blueprint to film the actual miniatures. Later, ILM artists would clean up the footage digitally, adding star fields, planets, and other key environmental details. In all, Knoll estimates that he completed about 36 different shots with the models, ranging from soaring space scenes to closeups at Adelphi Base.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-razor-crest-flying_b6b2f169.jpeg?region=0,0,1545,1080\" alt=\"The Razor Crest in flight.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eShiny and chrome\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBecause the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eseen in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eis a new model, it differs from the original in several key ways. It’s the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eequivalent of a retro car, one that rolled right off the assembly line and has been kept perfectly preserved in a garage.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“It’s meant to be clean and new, and it hasn’t been hot rodded the way Mando has customized it — like what \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/han-solo\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Han Solo\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHan Solo\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e did with the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eMillennium Falcon\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e,” Knoll explains. “This [new ship] is more in factory condition. The paint on the yellow stripe is fully intact. The finish on it is cleaner, so it’s a more shiny, bare metal finish — not quite as oxidized and aged as the one from Season 1.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThe shiny finish of the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eechoes the shiny \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/beskar\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"beskar\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003ebeskar\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e armor that Mando wears — but it also provided challenges for the crew. While shooting the miniatures, Knoll had to ensure that every reflection was perfect, monitoring how the light glinted off the body.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-razor-crest-lightin_0368cf1d.jpeg?region=0,0,1620,1080\" alt='The Razor Crest model filmed inside \"the gazebo.\"' title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eThe Razor Crest model filmed inside \"the gazebo.\"\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“Lighting is really tricky when it’s something that’s shiny,” Hickel adds. “You basically have to light it the way they light cars in TV commercials with big, broad panels of lights. You get a nice broad reflection that shows all the detail. You have to play with it because it’s all sort of make-believe. When the ship’s in space, theoretically there’s just a single light source out there somewhere, like a sun, but we do all kinds of tricks to get a nice rim light on one edge and a big swath of light on the other side. If it’s near a planet, you want whatever the general color of that planet is washing over it, whether it’s bluish or reddish or whatever. That reflectivity presents opportunities but also a lot of challenges.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIn an attempt to perfect the reflections on \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eseries, Knoll invented something he nicknamed “the gazebo,” a partially enclosed space made of foam boards. The miniature would be situated inside, and Knoll could project atmospheric images onto the walls of the gazebo, giving the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003emore accurate reflections. “It sort of worked,” Knoll admits. “It was hard to really calibrate the color on that.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eSo, for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu, \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eKnoll pitched an even more ambitious idea: What if they built a miniature version of an ILM StageCraft LED volume, allowing them to surround the miniatures with realistic environments?\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-razor-crest-john-go_8e59c480.jpeg?region=0,0,1620,1080\" alt=\"John Goodson on set with the 24-inch Razor Crest model.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eJohn Goodson on set with the 24-inch Razor Crest model.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-razor-crest-on-set_5759ca58.jpeg?region=0,0,1620,1080\" alt=\"The Razor Crest model filmed on set.  \" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eThe Razor Crest model filmed on set.  \u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThat way, the team could execute more miniature shots than ever before. For scenes on the sunny beaches of Adelphi Base, for example, Knoll would shoot the miniature outside in real sunlight. But with the volume, the team could swap out the background depending on what the shot needed, whether it was endless dark star fields or the thick clouds of the planet Nal Hutta.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-razor-crest-cockpit_a591e249.jpeg?region=0,0,1620,1080\" alt=\"Filming inside the Razor Crest for Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eFilming inside the Razor Crest for Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTaking flight\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eNot every shot of the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ewas completed with miniatures; some were rendered entirely through computer graphics animation (especially shots where the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eRazor Crest \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ehas to execute a complicated aerial maneuver or try to outrun a speeding enemy ship). But for the ILM team, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eprovided a unique opportunity to continue the company’s history of innovation. Not only did they find new ways to push digital technology further, but they also embraced the original hand-crafted techniques that have been a part of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e since the beginning.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“We don’t want to hinder ourselves and say, ‘We always have to shoot miniatures,’ or ‘It always has to be digital,’” Capogreco adds. “There are choices made along the way to go, ‘Well, that could be digital, and that could be practical.’ Having that flexibility was fantastic.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-razor-crest_27f12bd7.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1280\" alt=\"Din and Grogu inside the Razor Crest.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThe result, the team hopes, is an awe-inspiring adventure that feels as seamless as possible.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“I think it’s actually really important that you’re not going, ‘Is that a miniature? Is that CG?’” Capogreco says with a smile. “It’s almost indistinguishable, and I’m really proud of that.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003ca find yourself in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e There’s no \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/hyperdrive\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"hyperdrive\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003ehyperdrive\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e required — it’s simply filmmaker and \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Director Jon Favreau’s tucked away studio space. Just inside, a very lucky few were recently invited to step into a larger world: the still-standing set of the Adelphi Officer’s Lounge from \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. (But trust us, seeing \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e on the big screen is the next best thing.)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAs you open a normal-seeming door, you’re quickly greeted with a not-so-normal, 360-degree view of the Officer’s Lounge, filled with helmets, nods to past battles, and… games? “That’s the game from \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/tosche-station\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Tosche Station\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTosche Station\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e,” proudly recounts Andrew L. Jones, the movie’s production designer. “We took it from \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Book of \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eBoba\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e Fett\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e and put it here. It plays the game \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eSpace Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e on the top. That was the inspiration.” Another billiards-like game is also nearby, providing multiple opportunities for New Republic personnel to mingle.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/adelphi-base-main_e9ee98a5.jpeg?region=0,0,1620,1080\" alt=\"Adelphi Base\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image media-image-inline\" style=\"margin-left: 1rem; float: right; max-width: 40%;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-set-visit-06_17c8bcff.jpeg?region=0,278,1080,1391\" alt=\"At Adelphi Base there are hidden elements everywhere: starbird flags, a wing of a downed starship, even the dome of a TIE fighter.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAs first glimpsed in the third season of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, the sunny locale of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/adelphi-base\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAdelphi Base\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e is something that would already take your breath away. In the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eWars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e galaxy, it is an ocean-side retreat for New Republic pilots to regroup and refresh before their next mission. But in the real world, the very tactile set of this Officer’s Lounge — jammed with spoils of war and hidden mementos — is a step even above that. It is proof of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003efilmmaking magic.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eFavreau filmed many scenes from \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/series/the-mandalorian\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/series/the-book-of-boba-fett\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Book of Boba Fett\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, and more right here. When \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"The Mandalorian and Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e wrapped, he and his team decided to leave the Adelphi Base set up. After all, what’s better than a real sliver of a galaxy far, far away?\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThere are hidden elements everywhere: starbird flags, a wing of a downed starship, even the dome of a \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/tie-fighter\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"TIE fighter\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTIE fighter\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. “That’s the real one from Season 2,” says Jones. And, as the crew confirmed, some were even updated between the third season finale of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eand the opening scenes of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. The trophies had to be consistent with what had happened in-universe. “All the trophies and insignias have a whole story,” says Propmaster Josh Roth.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia-adelphi-base_4d6bfa1e.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The bar at Adelphi Base.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-cast-sweaver-adelph_5826435d.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1280\" alt=\"Mandalorian (Pedro Pascal) and Colonel Ward (Sigourney Weaver) in Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eMandalorian (Pedro Pascal) and Colonel Ward (Sigourney Weaver) in Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eA few cups of sparkling cold spotchka are laid out on the bar. The bartender may not be Snivvian, but the blue drink is refreshing nonetheless. As the crewmembers are happy to point out, a lot of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ehas happened in this room. In one corner is the booth where \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-mandalorian\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Din Djarin\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eDin Djarin\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e and \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eGrogu\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e met up with Sigourney Weaver’s Colonel Ward, as seen in the first trailer for the film. This spot at the bar is where we first met a live action Garazeb Orrelios in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, Season 3, Chapter 21: “The Pirate.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBut, if you get lucky, there also might be some \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003ereal \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBD droids (as seen by visitors to \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: Galaxy’s Edge\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e at Disney Parks) creating a little mischief and a lot of cuteness. The Mandalorian himself, Din Djarin, as well as his foundling, the little Grogu, have also been known to make an appearance at times. There is significant life in this room, especially when surrounded by droids and aliens. It feels \u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003elike \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eis really happening all around you\u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eA lot of that is because of the room’s meticulous design. As Jones says, “Everything that we can find and repurpose we do because it already has a language of manufacture that humans are familiar with. See those incense burners on the bar table? Those are sprinkler covers. That’s the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eWars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e way.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-set-visit-16_93fabee3.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1080\" alt=\"The familiar “IG heads” behind the Adelphi bar\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThis repurposing is an intrinsic part of how \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e movies have been made, ever since the original film, which turns 50 in 2027. The familiar “IG heads” behind the Adelphi bar were first glimpsed in a cantina on \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/tatooine\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Tatooine\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTatooine\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e in 1977 — once simply the combustion chamber of a Rolls Royce engine. (They were later \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003ere\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e-repurposed as the top of a fearsome droid bounty \u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003ehunter\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003e on the bridge of the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/executor\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Executor\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eExecutor\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e in 1980 when \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/ig-88\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"IG-88\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIG-88\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e made his debut in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/star-wars-episode-v-the-empire-strikes-back\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Empire Strikes Back\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e.) Everything in this room is manufactured, lived-in, and \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003ereal.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eA lucky few got to see this magic up close, but now we all get to experience it on the big screen in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu. \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAnd, honestly, it’s just a comfort knowing that there’s that sliver of a galaxy far, far away somewhere here on Earth.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.fandango.com/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-2026-242515/movie-overview\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eGet your Presley.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eWith lithe limbs and a round metallic hat that can protect against enemy fire or be wielded as a weapon, the Kyuzo bounty h\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003eunter\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003e has a striking physique. Fans of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/series/star-wars-the-clone-wars\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Star Wars: The Clone Wars\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Clone Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e first met Embo in the Season 2 episode \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/series/clone-wars/bounty-hunters-episode-guide\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“Bounty Hunters,”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e when he and the rest of Sugi’s crew joined forces with the Jedi \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/anakin-skywalker\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Anakin Skywalker\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAnakin Skywalker\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/obi-wan-kenobi\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Obi-Wan Kenobi\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eObi-Wan Kenobi\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, and \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/ahsoka-tano\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Ahsoka Tano\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAhsoka Tano\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. In an homage to Akira Kurosawa’s \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eSeven Samari,\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Embo was one of seven surprising allies who helped teach a village of humble farmers to defend themselves against \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/hondo-ohnaka\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Hondo Ohnaka\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHondo Ohnaka\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e and his pirates.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIn his animated introduction, Embo quickly showcased his lethal skill with his \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/bowcaster\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Bowcaster\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003ebowcaster\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e and his bare hands. But Lucasfilm President and Chief Creative Officer \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.lucasfilm.com/leadership/dave-filoni/\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eDave Filoni\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e reveals that Embo was always destined for live action, dating back to a piece of concept art created two decades ago\u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003e.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e “While we were writing and creating \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Clone Wars, \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eGeorge [Lucas] was also developing a live action series called \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eUnderworld\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e,” Filoni tells StarWars.com. “He had a lot of visual development done where he was exploring new designs for ships, planets, droids and aliens. When we would meet to discuss upcoming \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eClone Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e[episodes], George would use some of that visual inspiration for our stories.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eOn one particular day, Lucas shared a piece of concept art for an alien bounty hunter. “It was very rough,” Filoni recalls. “He had the large round hat but many of the details were unresolved.” The mysterious bounty hunter had yet to be named Embo, but Lucas and Filoni both loved the design and wanted to incorporate it into the “Bounty Hunters” episode. “I gave Embo the species name ‘Kyuzo’ which was a character from the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eSeven Samurai\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e played by Seiji Miyaguchi,” Filoni adds. “I really liked that character so I gave a nod to the performance in Embo's character.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/who-is-embo-marrok-tcw_e25211b3.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,811\" alt=\"Embo and Marrok in The Clone Wars.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\u003cb class=\"bolds\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA loyal companion\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image media-image-inline\" style=\"margin-left: 1rem; float: right; max-width: 36%;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/who-is-embo-dave-filoni-concept-art_26dfa55c.jpeg?region=0,0,859,1080\" alt=\"Concept art of Embo and Marrok from The Clone Wars by Dave Filoni.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eConcept art of Embo and Marrok from The Clone Wars by Dave Filoni.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAs Embo made more regular appearances, he gained an anooba companion named Marrok. “[Concept artist] Pat Presley took that rough design and refined it and I gave Embo the dog,” Filoni says. Well known for his appreciation of wolves and other animals, the anooba was a nod to one of Filoni’s favorite characters from another franchise, G.I. Joe’s \"Snake Eyes,\" who has a dog named Timber. “I always liked that combination of a warrior and dog,” Filoni says.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBeyond the G.I. Joe inspiration, Embo’s original anooba was also steeped in Earthbound legends. “The name Marrok comes from Arthurian Legend and a story called ‘Sir Marrok: A Tale of the Days of King Arthur’ by Allen French,” Filoni reveals. “In the story, a knight of Arthur's round table returns from the Crusades and is transformed into a wolf by a witch who has taken over his kingdom.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eEmbo and Marrok made several appearances over the years in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Clone Wars, \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ewith ties to \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/jabba-the-hutt\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Jabba the Hutt\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eJabba the Hutt\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e and a paying gig as security detail for the Grand \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/hutt\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Hutt\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHutt\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Council amid the rise of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/Maul\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Maul\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eMaul\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e’s \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/shadow-collective\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Shadow Collective\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eShadow Collective\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, several jobs with young \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/boba-fett\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Boba Fett\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBoba Fett\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e’s crew,  and an assignment targeting political enemy \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/rush-clovis\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Rush Clovis\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eRush Clovis\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e for Darth Sidious (just to name a few).\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/who-is-embo-keibu_c8e8751e.jpeg?region=0,105,1545,975\" alt=\"Keibu in The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIn \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"The Mandalorian and Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, we meet Embo in a new era, the age of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-new-republic\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"The New Republic\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003ethe New Republic\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. The times have changed, along with Embo’s companion, but his loyalty still remains up for sale. “I figured that Marrok was probably no longer around by the time of the film, so we gave Embo a new dog named Keibu,” Filoni notes, before teasing “I did come up with a story about what happened to Marrok so maybe one day we can share that somehow.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e‘Business is business’\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eFiloni has long been the voice of Embo, but to bring the animated hunter to live action, his physical form was rendered through computer animation by \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.ilm.com/\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIndustrial Light \u0026amp; Magic\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. \"His motion is based on stunt performer Donald Mills’ actions, with heavy modification by our ILM animation team to account for Embo’s height,” the film’s Animation Supervisor Hal Hickel says. Hickel, Filoni notes, also spoke with Lucasfilm Animation Director Keith Kellogg and the rest of the legacy \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eClone Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e team to ensure the character stayed true to form.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/who-is-embo-concept-art_b6f696f3.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,803\" alt=\"\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eConcept art of Embo and Keibu for The Mandalorian and Grogu by Nick Gindraux.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIt’s just one example of the collaboration that seamlessly blends the physical puppets and practical ships and real environments with CG elements, ships, aliens, and creatures in \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. “In a fun moment, Embo does a touch of his hat in the movie, which is something he did in animation,” Filoni says, “so I think there was a lot of great observation and care that went into bringing Embo to life.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/who-is-embo-the-mandalorian_d522318d.jpeg?region=0,0,1545,1080\" alt=\"\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAnd while Embo is something of a ruthless rogue, he inhabits a gray area in the continuum of good versus evil in the galaxy. “Embo has always been portrayed as neither a good guy nor a bad guy,” Filoni says. “I think he respects Mando as a hunter, but business is business.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAnd Embo’s business is capturing his target and getting paid.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.fandango.com/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-2026-242515/movie-overview\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eGet your tickets\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e for Lucasfilm’s \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, an all-new \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eadventure filmed for IMAX, in theaters She was 80.\u003c/span\u003e","summary":"\u003ch2\u003e\u003cspan\u003eMarcia Lucas, one of three editors who won an Academy Award for their work on the original \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e film, has died. She was 80.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e","main_content":"\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image media-image-inline\" style=\"margin-left: 1rem; float: right; max-width: 40%;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/starwarcom-marcia-lucas_a9a93f37.jpeg?region=0,0,858,1080\" alt=\"Richard Chew, Marcia Lucas, and Paul Hirsch win the Academy Award for Best Film Editing.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eRichard Chew, Marcia Lucas, and Paul Hirsch win the Academy Award for Best Film Editing.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eLucasfilm was deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Marcia Lucas. The 80-year-old was one of the three editors to take home an Oscar for 1977’s \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: A New Hope\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAfter Lucasfilm’s establishment in 1971, production began on George Lucas’ newest feature film, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eAmerican Graffiti\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e (1973). Marcia Lucas joined her mentor Verna Fields as editor of the film, for which the pair received an Oscar nomination. Marcia then worked for director Martin Scorsese on \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eAlice Doesn’t Live Here Anymore \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e(1974) and \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eTaxi Driver \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e(1976) as Lucasfilm readied \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: A New Hope\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAs the film entered post-production, George Lucas found that a near total restart was required, and Richard Chew and Paul Hirsch joined the editorial team with Marcia, who eventually departed to work on Scorsese’s \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eNew York, New York \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e(1977). Along with Chew and Hirsch, she would go on to win the Oscar for \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003ein 1978. \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIn succeeding years, Marcia contributed to other Lucasfilm productions, including \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eMore American Graffiti \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e(1979), \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Empire Strikes Back \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e(1980), and \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: Return of the Jedi \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e(1983), among others. \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“I love film editing,” Marcia once told a reporter. “I have an innate ability to take good material and make it better, and to take bad material and make it fair.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eLucasfilm joins the global filmmaking community in mourning the loss of Marcia Lucas.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e"},"publish_date":"May 30, 2026","publish_date_short":"May 30","content_date":"2026-05-29T19:24:46-07:00","publish_date_diff":"131 days More","images":{"thumb_images":{"thumb_baseball_card":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg?region=13%2C174%2C634%2C825","thumb_4x3":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg?region=0%2C202%2C697%2C524","thumb_1x1":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg?region=92%2C203%2C502%2C502","thumb_2x3":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg?region=80%2C174%2C495%2C742"}},"thumb_images":{"thumb_baseball_card":{"src":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg?region=13,174,634,825","base_src":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg","width":634,"height":825,"aspect_ratio":1.3013,"aspect_ratio_pct":"130.13%","orientation":"portrait","half_width":317,"half_height":413},"thumb_4x3":{"src":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg?region=0,202,697,524","base_src":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg","width":697,"height":524,"aspect_ratio":0.7518,"aspect_ratio_pct":"75.18%","orientation":"landscape","half_width":349,"half_height":262},"thumb_1x1":{"src":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg?region=92,203,502,502","base_src":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg","width":502,"height":502,"aspect_ratio":1.0,"aspect_ratio_pct":"100.0%","orientation":"landscape","half_width":251,"half_height":251},"thumb_2x3":{"src":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg?region=80,174,495,742","base_src":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg","width":495,"height":742,"aspect_ratio":1.499,"aspect_ratio_pct":"149.9%","orientation":"portrait","half_width":248,"half_height":371}},"thumb_data":{"src":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg?region=13,174,634,825","base_src":"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/kristin-baver-headshot_df340e97.jpeg","width":634,"height":825,"aspect_ratio":1.3013,"aspect_ratio_pct":"130.13%","orientation":"portrait","half_width":317,"half_height":413},"alt_text":"Kristin
