Closer Look at Grogu - Star of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e","headline":"\u003ch2\u003e\u003cspan\u003eA Closer Look at Grogu - Star of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e","summary_stripped":"\u003cspan\u003eWe’d follow Grogu anywhere. The puppeteers who create the complex illusion already do.\u003c/span\u003e","summary":"\u003ch2\u003e\u003cspan\u003eWe’d follow Grogu anywhere. The puppeteers who create the complex illusion already do.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e","main_content":"\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThe world was watching as \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eGrogu\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e toddled onto the red carpet at the Hollywood premiere of \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/films/Star-Wars-The-Mandalorian-and-Grogu\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e last week.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eInstead of a designer suit, the diminutive star wore the simple brown coat that’s become his signature look. He didn’t need a chic frock or hair and makeup; the pink apple cheeks are all natural, his wispy hair always appearing freshly washed and perfectly wild.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv mh-tiktok-node-alignment=\"center\" mh-tiktok-node-src=\"https://www.tiktok.com/@starwars/video/7640126097509715231\" class=\"mh-tiktok\" style=\"justify-content: center; display: flex;\"\u003e\n\u003cblockquote class=\"tiktok-embed\" data-video-id=\"7640126097509715231\" data-embed-from=\"oembed\" cite=\"https://www.tiktok.com/@starwars/video/7640126097509715231\" style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 0px; max-width: 325px;\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.tiktok.com/@starwars/video/7640126097509715231\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cscript src=\"https://www.tiktok.com/embed.js\" id=\"mh-social-widget-script\" async=\"\"\u003e\u003c/script\u003e\n\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAnd yet, in a sea of top talent including Director Jon Favreau and co-stars Pedro Pascal (the titular Mandalorian \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/the-mandalorian\" tabindex=\"0\" class=\"a-rich-article\" aria-label=\"Din Djarin\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eDin Djarin\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e) and Sigourney Weaver (\u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.starwars.com/databank/colonel-ward\" target=\"_self\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eColonel Ward\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e), Grogu invariably stole the show. He smiled and cooed, waving for the cameras and striking a variety of photoshoot-perfect poses like an absolute pro.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eOf course, Legacy Effects has worked behind the scenes for nearly a decade to perfect the practical puppet that anchors Grogu’s performance and very existence, in collaboration with the visual effects wizards at Industrial Light \u0026amp; Magic. “The advances in animatronics and robotics combined with the advances in CG just brings new life to characters that might have been a very traditional approach,” says Legacy Effects Co-Founder Alan Scott, “but then they’re just elevated to the next level.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-teaser-trailer-stil_457b4046.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,803\" alt=\"Grogu in Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIn a creature shop with about 100 employees, a character of Grogu’s caliber incorporates work from the entire studio to bring the practical puppet to life, Scott reveals. “Everyone touches it, whether it is sculpting, digital design, 3D printing, molding, casting, all of it matters. Every one of those little steps are combined to create the end result. It’s the artistry of everyone combined that creates what you think of as one singular character but it takes a lot of people.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-jon-favreau-intervi_5999898e.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1280\" alt=\"Director Jon Favreau and Pedro Pascal on the set of Star Wars:The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eDirector Jon Favreau and Pedro Pascal on the set of Star Wars:The Mandalorian and Grogu.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAnd that’s just the upfront work to build the animatronic. On every shoot day and every special event where Grogu has made an appearance, a team of skilled puppeteers works tirelessly off-camera to ensure that Grogu can hold his own, performing with his incredibly talented co-stars. “It’s easy for it to fall apart,” Scott admits. “Basically, it’s like we’ve built this amazing instrument and now we have to learn how to play it. It’s not one person because there’s so many different functionalities; ultimately four or five or sometimes more people are using their performance to create one singular performance. And the more that you work together, the more that you learn what the puppet is capable of, the more intuitive and natural those become.”\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-jon-favreau-intervi_011b6617.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1280\" alt=\"Director Jon Favreau and Pedro Pascal on the set of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eDirector Jon Favreau and Pedro Pascal on the set of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBack in Season 1 of the Disney+ series \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, where the duo of \u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003ethe Manda\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003elorian a\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003end Grogu\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan\u003e first took the world and the galaxy by storm, a tradition of speaking directly to Grogu when directing him began, treating the little child star like every other actor on set. That continued during filming on the theatrical standalone adventure. “[Jon Favreau] directs the puppet and then everyone knows what their responsibility is,” Scott says, referencing the core crew of puppeteers — Mike Manzel, Dawn Diniger, Jason Matthews, Trevor Hensley, and Victor Broadley — operating Grogu. On days when the film’s four Anzellans were in the mix, there could be as many as 25 puppeteers on set to bring all five characters to life.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv mh-tiktok-node-alignment=\"center\" mh-tiktok-node-src=\"https://www.tiktok.com/@starwars/video/7646905277408726303\" class=\"mh-tiktok\" style=\"justify-content: center; display: flex;\"\u003e\n\u003cblockquote class=\"tiktok-embed\" data-video-id=\"7646905277408726303\" data-embed-from=\"oembed\" cite=\"https://www.tiktok.com/@starwars/video/7646905277408726303\" style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 0px; max-width: 325px;\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.tiktok.com/@starwars/video/7646905277408726303\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cscript src=\"https://www.tiktok.com/embed.js\" id=\"mh-social-widget-script\" async=\"\"\u003e\u003c/script\u003e\n\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThe final version of the shots seen in the film may be augmented by ILM, but there’s no post-production involved in a live event like a red carpet strut. But when it comes to a scene in the movie, even Scott and his crew can’t always tell where the puppet ends and the CG begins, a seamless blend of techniques that gives Grogu his full range of articulation and emotion.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/choose-your-mandalorian-clan-mudhorn_4be935ce.jpeg?region=0,0,1280,535\" alt=\"Grogu and Din Djarin in Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-teaser-trailer-stil_1a2620e1.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,804\" alt=\"Grogu and the Mandalorian in Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIn real life and in the story, Grogu is always evolving. For the film, the puppet had to be able to swim and do other stunt work, including perching on the Mandalorian’s shoulder during action-packed sequences “He wants Grogu to grow,” Scott says of Favreau. “He’s got a story to tell. The baby is much more active [in the film]. He’s basically now a little protégé to Mando. [Favreau] wanted him to be able to live in Mando’s shoes and work with him and train with him and be his little apprentice in an interesting way that was still naïve and child-like but at the same time served the story.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003e“This is an action movie,” Scott continues. “There’s lots of fights. There’s lots of stunts. Where is the child during all of that?” Always right by Din Djarin’s side, armored up and ready for whatever the galaxy throws at him.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"media-image\" style=\"text-align: center; max-width: 100%; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;\"\u003e\u003cfigure\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/images/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-interview-premiere_c474b082.jpeg?region=0,0,1920,1280\" alt=\"Sigourney Weaver, Pedro Pascal, Grogu, Jon Favreau, Dave Filoni at the World Premiere of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\" title=\"\"\u003e\u003cfigcaption style=\" text-align: center;\"\u003eSigourney Weaver, Pedro Pascal, Grogu, Jon Favreau, Dave Filoni at the World Premiere of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.\u003c/figcaption\u003e\u003c/figure\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eBut when you’re gazing upon Grogu, whether he’s interacting with Favreau and his co-stars on the press tour or in the incredibly fun tale unfolding in his big-screen debut, it’s easy to forget all that. One can imagine that instead of those puppeteers, Grogu is like all the other actors during filming, breaking for lunch with his friends the Anzellans and napping on a towering director’s chair in between shots.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThe first one on set. Always on his mark. Always ready for action.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.fandango.com/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-2026-242515/movie-overview\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eGet your tickets\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e for Lucasfilm’s \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe Mandalorian and Grogu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003e, an all-new \u003c/span\u003e\u003ci\u003e\u003cem\u003eStar Wars \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/i\u003e\u003cspan\u003eadventure filmed for IMAX, in theaters now.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e"},"publish_date":"May 28, 2026","publish_date_short":"May **AGENT:** The newest announced **Star Wars film** is **_Star Wars: Starfighter_**.

- **Director:** Shawn Levy  
- **Star:** Ryan Gosling as Kade Auberon  
- **Release date:** **May 28, 2027**
- **Story:** A standalone adventure set in a previously unexplored period of the Star Wars timeline. It follows a cynical rogue whose mysterious past draws him into a dangerous galaxy-spanning adventure.
- **Other announced cast:** Matt Smith, Mia Goth, Aaron Pierre, Jamael Westman, Daniel Ings, Flynn Gray, and Amy Adams.

The latest official update I found says Disney and Lucasfilm revealed the film’s logo at D23 and described it as the next theatrical Star Wars feature. StarWars.com also reports that it was filmed for IMAX.

[Official StarWars.com announcement](https://www.starwars.com/news/star-wars-starfighter-ryan-gosling)
